title: How many CPD points do healthcare professionals need to renew a DHA license in Dubai?
description: Dubai Health Authority CPD rules for license renewal: annual points by profession, the 70 percent specialty rule, excluded activities and penalties.
shortAnswer: Under the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) Manual for Licensing Healthcare Professionals, version 1.4 effective September 30, 2026, licensed professionals must earn CPD points every year: 40 for physicians and dentists, 20 for nurses and pharmacists, and 10 for allied health and traditional, complementary and integrative medicine practitioners. At least 70 percent must be in the professional's specialty, points do not carry forward, and a license cannot be renewed until the target is met.
keyTakeaways: Annual CPD targets follow the Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements (PQR): 40 points for physicians and dentists, 20 for nurses, 20 for pharmacists and 10 for allied health and TCIM practitioners.
Multi year licenses multiply the target: a physician renewing for three years must upload 120 points to the Sheryan licensing system before the license expires.

At least 70 percent of points must be in the area of the professional specialty and up to 30 percent can be general professional development; all points may be earned online if specialty related and recognized.
Ward rounds, internal departmental meetings, induction and orientation, software skills and basic product training do not count toward the target.
Missing CPD blocks renewal and suspends the right to practice until compliance; penalties for late renewal are the responsibility of both the professional and the employing facility.
regulator: Dubai Health Authority (DHA), Health Regulation Sector, Health Licensing Department
appliesTo: Physicians, dentists, nurses, pharmacists, allied health professionals and TCIM practitioners holding a DHA professional license
Dubai health facilities that renew their professionals' licenses and employ them
Medical directors responsible for licensing compliance in a facility
Medical education, HR and credentialing teams that track CPD

sections.heading: Which DHA rules set CPD requirements for license renewal?

blocks.text: Two instruments set the requirement. The Manual for Licensing Healthcare Professionals (code DHA/HRS/HLD/MA-2), version 1.4, issued and effective on September 30, 2026, contains the renewal rules in chapter 11 and the CPD rules in chapter 14 ([DHA Manual for Licensing Healthcare Professionals](https://www.dha.gov.ae/attachments/regulatoryDocuments/1790949482460-374216735.pdf)). Section 18.1 of the manual ties the targets to the Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements (PQR), issued jointly by the Ministry of Health and Prevention, the Department of Health Abu Dhabi, DHA and the Sharjah Health Authority, in its April 2025 edition ([Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements](https://www.doh.gov.ae/-/media/D112FF75EF0140439A733B16081292DF.ashx)).

The manual defines continuing professional development as the learning activities through which professionals maintain and develop their knowledge and skills to practice safely, effectively and legally, and notes that CPD is also referred to as continuing medical education (CME). Version 1.4's summary of changes states that chapter 11 now establishes that CPD non compliance prevents license renewal and practice and may incur penalties and arrears. This page describes the rules as at November 2026.

Professionals licensed in Abu Dhabi follow a different emirate level CPD standard, described in [Department of Health Abu Dhabi CPD requirements](/regulations/doh-abu-dhabi-cme-requirements). For an Australian comparison, see the [Ahpra CPD registration standards](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards).

sections.heading: How many CPD points are required each year by profession?

blocks.text: Section 15.3 of the manual sets the annual target, and section 18.1 repeats it as required by the PQR. Section 18.3 adds that a professional licensed in more than one category, whether full time or part time, is measured against the category with the highest target.

blocks.text: Section 15.2 allows renewal for one, two or three years, and sections 18.10 and 18.11 double or triple the target accordingly, with the points uploaded to Sheryan, the Dubai Health Licensing System, before renewal. The manual's own example is a physician renewing for three years, who must submit 120 points before the license expires. Section 18.9 says points earned above the target cannot be carried forward or transferred from a previous year.

sections.heading: What counts toward the DHA CPD target, and what does not?

blocks.text: Activities must be mainly in the professional's specialty and recognized by the relevant authorities. Section 18.5 requires that at least 70 percent of the target be in the area of the professional specialty, with up to 30 percent in general professional development. Section 18.6 allows 100 percent of the target to be earned through online programs, and section 18.8 accepts online points as long as they relate to the specialty and are recognized by relevant authorities.

items: **Counts:** participation in a DHA assessment panel for licensing professionals is accepted as part of the calendar year's CPD (section 18.12).

**Does not count (section 18.13):** regular morning meetings, endorsements, ward rounds and case revisions; departmental or medical society internal meetings; community and patient awareness sessions; public directed activities; software skills training; induction and orientation programs; and basic product training or product specific knowledge.

blocks.text: The exclusions matter for facility training teams. Mandatory in-house programs such as orientation, electronic medical record training and device in-servicing are still required for safe practice and accreditation, but they will not reduce a professional's CPD target. Tracking them separately avoids a common audit finding where completion of internal training is mistaken for licensure CPD. Version 1.4's change summary also notes that accredited training hours are not required for eligible trainees.

sections.heading: What happens if a professional has not met the CPD target at renewal?

blocks.text: The license is not renewed and the professional cannot practice until the target is met. Section 15.5 states that failure to meet the required points results in rejection of the renewal application and suspension of the right to practice until compliance is achieved. Section 18.4 makes CPD completion a prerequisite for renewal.

items: **Penalties for delay:** section 15.6 states that delays in renewal caused by CPD non compliance attract applicable penalties that must be paid in full, and that both the professional and the employing facility bear full responsibility for the consequences.
**Renewal window:** section 15.4 requires the health facility to apply for renewal within three months of the license expiry date.

**False claims:** section 18.2 treats fraudulent, falsified, misleading or unverifiable CPD as a breach that may lead to suspension or revocation, and section 18.14 refers fraudulent CPD claims to the Medical Professional Committee for disciplinary action.
**Verification:** section 18.15 lets DHA require primary source verification or confirmation from the issuing body to check that certificates are authentic and accredited.

blocks.title: Why facilities share the risk
blocks.text: Because the facility applies for renewal and shares responsibility for delay penalties, a Dubai employer cannot treat CPD as purely the professional's affair. A facility level tracker that flags shortfalls several months before expiry is the practical control.

sections.heading: How does CPD apply to professionals returning after a break in practice?

blocks.text: A larger one time CPD requirement applies. Section 1.7 of the PQR states that professionals with a discontinuity in clinical practice of more than three years must complete specified CME/CPD credits and supervised training, related to their specialty, before licensure, and that most non UAE nationals cannot apply after a gap of more than five years.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures a facility's education offering against each professional category, specialty and the DHA counting rules, so every activity is tagged as specialty CPD, general CPD or non qualifying internal training before it is delivered. That makes the 70 percent rule and the exclusions in section 18.13 checkable from the framework rather than at renewal.

faqs.q: Can all DHA CPD points be earned online?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 18.6 of the DHA licensing manual allows 100 percent of the target to come from online programs, provided under section 18.8 that they relate to the professional's specialty field and are recognized by the relevant authorities. The 70 percent specialty rule still applies to online activities.

faqs.q: Do extra CPD points carry over to the next year in Dubai?
faqs.a: No. Section 18.9 states that a professional who overachieves the target is not eligible to carry points forward, and points cannot be transferred from a previous year. For two and three year licenses, the multiplied target applies across the whole license period.

faqs.q: Does hospital orientation or EMR training count as CPD?
faqs.a: No. Section 18.13 excludes induction and orientation programs, software skills training, basic product training and internal departmental meetings. These may still be mandatory for the facility, but they do not count toward the professional's DHA CPD target.

faqs.q: Who is responsible if a renewal is delayed because CPD is incomplete?
faqs.a: Both. Section 15.6 states that penalties arising from CPD related delays must be settled in full and that both the professional and the employing health facility bear full responsibility for the consequences of non compliance with DHA regulations.

Section 15.2 renewal for 1, 2 or 3 years; 15.3 annual CPD of 40 for physicians and dentists, 20 nurses, 10 allied and TCIM, 20 pharmacists, cumulative for multi year licenses (example 120 for a 3 year physician license); 15.4 facility applies within three months of expiry; 15.5 failure results in rejection and suspension of the right to practice; 15.6 penalties, joint responsibility of professional and facility.

Chapter 14: 18.1 targets per PQR; 18.2 fraudulent CPD may lead to suspension or revocation; 18.3 highest category applies; 18.4 prerequisite for renewal; 18.5 at least 70 percent specialty and 30 percent general; 18.6 100 percent online allowed; 18.8 online accepted if specialty related and recognized; 18.9 no carry forward; 18.10 and 18.11 doubled or tripled and uploaded in Sheryan; 18.12 DHA assessment panel counts; 18.13 excluded activities; 18.14 MPC disciplinary action; 18.15 PSV of certificates.

PQR (April 2025) issued by MOHAP, DOH, DHA and SHA; section 2.2 minimum annual CME/CPD: physicians and dentists 40, nurses 20, pharmacists 20, allied health 10, TCIM 10; section 1.7 gap of practice over 3 years requires 80/40/20, 120/60/30 or 200/100/50 credits with 6, 8 or 12 months of training; non UAE nationals generally cannot apply after a gap over 5 years.
